I've written 4 review comments to `comments.json` (the JSON is valid). The fix only partly closes the race, and the new test may pass without ever triggering it.

**About the diff:** the PR's actual change is small: `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` plus one new test in `GroupTest`. Most of the diff against the base commit is unrelated noise, probably because the branch is stale. It includes JGroups config, docs, `kc.sh`/`kc.bat`, token-exchange tests and a `ConsentScopeRepresentation` rename, and I didn't review any of that.

**Findings:**

1. **`GroupAdapter.java:275` – the method can now return null.** The `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` Javadoc says it "Never returns null", but the fix returns null when the group is deleted mid-read. That null ends up in `GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount`, where it looks the same as "count not requested". Any caller that unboxes it just gets the NPE somewhere else. Returning `0L` would be safer, or better, skipping groups that have disappeared.
2. **`GroupAdapter.java:256` (and lines 262, 268) – the same NPE is still there.** All three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. A concurrent delete will still crash those paths.
3. **`GroupTest.java:139` – the new test is unreliable.**
   - The reader thread is never joined, and nothing makes sure it is running before the deletions start. So the test can pass without the race ever happening.
   - Exceptions thrown after `deletedAll` is set are added after the assertion runs, so they're missed.
   - If `remove()` throws, the thread loops against the server for the rest of the suite.
4. **`GroupTest.java:143` – may not test the changed code at all.** Unless this endpoint turns subgroup counts on by default, it never calls `getSubGroupsCount()`. I didn't check that default, so I left it as a question. The comment also points out the `groupUuuids` typo.

I didn't build the code or run any tests.
